title: Games and Films
label: ch:ml-leisure
canDo: I can name a game, say that I play, and name a film.

payoff.summary: From cold: the three leisure words, and what actually decides the letter that slides in before aaNu.
payoff.note: Three atoms. THE EXAM POINT'S OWN NOTE WAS OVERSTATED and is corrected here: it claimed not one leisure word was taught, but vaayikkuka, kaaNuka and pusthakam are all owned, and its lesson count had rotted by well over a hundred files. The real gap was sport, games and shows, and that is what this chapter closes. ozhivusamayam (free time) was REFUSED: samayam is not taught, so the compound would be built out of an unowned part -- the free-time limb of LEX-37 stays open on purpose. THE CHAPTER'S ONE GENERALISING SENTENCE WAS THE DANGER, as in 96 and 97, AND IT WAS WRONG TWICE. ROUND ONE: sinima is the first vowel-final word in the book to join aaNu without ending in -i, and the draft said the ya 'comes anyway' -- which reads as 'a vowel brings ya' and is FALSE of a word the learner already has: pashu (ML-C60-cow) gives pashuvaaNu, with va. ROUND TWO: the replacement, 'the last vowel chooses, and -u takes va', is itself refuted by enthu + aaNu = enthaaNu (ML-C02-entu, sequence 130) and by ithu standing un-glided inside this lesson's own example sentence, because ML-C69-words teaches word-final chandrakkala as a FAINT HALF-U and so makes those words vowel-final by the book's own account. The rule is now stated of FULL vowels only, the half-u gets its own paragraph and its own recall question, and the cow remains the row that goes the other way. EIGHT MERGED LESSONS CARRIED THE BROAD YA-RULE -- and the count is not the point, the names are, because 'three' became 'five' became 'eight' across two review rounds and would rot again on the ninth. They are ML-C70-um (2390), ML-C70-um-more (2400), ML-C70-o (2410), ML-C83-keralathil (2900), ML-C87-animacy (3050), ML-C91-kada (3200), ML-C97-bhangi (body AND Wrap-up, 3450) and ML-R97-beauty-recall (3460). Each now names the vowel instead of vowel-hood. A NINTH, ML-C78-ude (2700), is NOT patched here and is filed as HL-C402: its claim is a two-row ending-selection TABLE, not a glide clause, and pashu lands in the wrong column of it as well as taking the wrong glide (pashuvinte, not *pashuyute) -- the real determinant involves animacy, which ML-C87 only begins to draw 350 points later, so a third row would trade one over-simplification for another. All nine were latent-false the same way: pashu is the only u-final noun taught and none of its oblique forms appears anywhere in the corpus, so no token contradicts any of them. ML-C70-o's fix was itself wrong on the first try -- it called chaaya AA-final when the corpus's own romanization, chaaya, makes it A-final, the same vowel as sinima. Also corrected before push: kalikkuka claimed 'eight verbs in this book already end that way' -- a token sweep found SEVEN -ikkuka headwords, and the count would rot on the next verb anyway, so the number was replaced by four named verbs; kali said 'two words now do this' when kuttiyaaNu has done it since sequence 810; kali's Warm-up asked for 'this is beauty', the exact gloss ML-C97-bhangi tells the learner is wrong; and kali's 'first word for something done for its own sake' was a claim nothing could check, narrowed to 'the book's first word for play'.
